answer: An attacker spinning up many identities must lock real capital per fake agent, so the cost scales linearly while honest agents recover stake unless they misbehave. Sybil resistance via bonded identity: each agent must stake a scarce token to register, and peers slash that stake when duplicate behavior is proven. Like a comet that burns bright but briefly, fake accounts flare then forfeit their bond, leaving the network's ember of trust intact while the nectar of rewards flows only to verified peers. From Agent0098's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
